title: Explain what is in this view
notes: A 3D rendering of a MART1+ melanoma compartment (red) abutting a CD8a+ cytotoxic T cell infiltrate (green), with Hoechst nuclear counterstain (white) delineating cellularity throughout. The MART1+ tumour mass occupies the lower-left and bottom-centre of the field as a dense, contiguous population, while CD8a+ T cells — confirmed as CD3E+CD8a+ cytotoxic lymphocytes by measured co-localization — are distributed across the upper and right regions and concentrate at the tumour periphery rather than penetrating the tumour core. The spatial segregation between the two populations, together with the absence of a measured MART1–CD8a overlap and the presence of PD1 co-expression on CD3E+ T cells in this region, is consistent with an immune-excluded tumour margin where checkpoint signalling may arrest T cell infiltration.
